pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an underlying Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of psychiatric onset progressing to severe orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and the pathognomonic 'Extreme Delta Brush' pattern on EEG, prompting a pelvic ultrasound that revealed a mature cystic ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue expressed within an ovarian teratoma triggers the host immune system to generate IgG antibodies directed against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of NMDA receptors. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and cause selective cross-linking, internalization, and degradation of cell-surface NMDA receptors. The resulting profound reduction in NMDA-mediated synaptic transmission abolishes inhibitory GABAergic pathways, causing catastrophic frontostriatal disruption, psychiatric breakdown, dyskinesias, dysautonomia, and hypoventilation.
